```
ON-CALL HANDOFF — gateway 503s, 2026-03-14

ROOT CAUSE
dep-4471 set gateway.pool.perRequest: false -> true ("connection-per-request
for pool isolation"). Every request now takes its own pooled connection, so a
20-connection pool saturates under normal traffic. Gateway logged the flip at
02:13:41.234Z; first 503 followed 37s later. Failures are 1:1 with
ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED (530 each). Queue depth peaked at 271 waiters.

  ERROR access req-07401 /v1/cart -> billing-svc 503 659ms
  ERROR pool   req-07401 ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED acquiring connection from pool
        (size 20, in_use 20, waiting 74)

IMPACT WINDOW
Start  2026-03-14T02:14:18.972Z
End    ongoing at log end, 2026-03-14T03:59:27.974Z (1h45m)
Rate   530 of 636 requests failed, 83%
Scope  all five /v1 routes, all four upstreams. /health unaffected.
        Log is node-3 of 3. Other two nodes not checked — assume same.
Also   212 "acquire slow" warns on /v1/checkout and /v1/profile.

ROLL BACK
dep-4471, gateway, a.novak, finished 02:14:00Z.
Revert gateway.pool.perRequest to false. Note the same deploy raised
gateway.timeout.upstreamMs 2000 -> 2500; revert both together.

NOT THE CAUSE
dep-4472 (billing-svc 02:41) and dep-4473 (catalog-svc 03:20) both landed
after onset. Workers are clean: 0 errors, 0 failed jobs, db_wait max 12ms.
Worker job time drifted 200ms -> 2324ms but climbed steadily from 01:00 with
no step at onset. One known warn, OPS-2210, unindexed scan on orders.
```

Root cause and rollback target are the same deploy. Impact window is still open at log end.
